close_reason: Replaced four lossy 'as' narrowing casts in helpers.rs with try_from. now_utc_string: u64→i64 secs widened via i64::try_from with a 'clock-out-of-range' sentinel-string return path for corrupted clocks (~292 billion years past/before epoch). Pre-epoch negation uses .checked_neg() to avoid the i64::MIN underflow path. civil_from_days: i64→i32 year, i64→u8 month, i64→u8 day all converted to try_from(...).expect(...) with rationale strings documenting the algorithm-guaranteed bounds. No behavioural change on legitimate input; the cast-site panic on corrupted input is now an explicit expect rather than a silent wrap.
description: src/helpers.rs:67,72,101 use 'as' for narrowing casts: 'd.as_secs() as i64' (u64→i64, wraps to negative at 2^63 seconds), 'yr as i32' (i64→i32), 'mo as u8' and 'd as u8' (i64→u8). The 'as' operator silently truncates/wraps on overflow; clippy's cast_possible_truncation/cast_sign_loss/cast_possible_wrap families flag exactly these patterns. Idiomatic Rust uses i64::try_from(u) for fallible conversions or, when bounds are algorithm-guaranteed, u8::try_from(...).expect('bounded by algorithm to [1,12]'). What goes wrong if it stays: a silent year-wrap or month-overflow on a malformed SystemTime input becomes a bizarre RFC 3339 string instead of an explicit panic at the cast site. The narrowing of mo/d/yr is provably-safe by algorithm, so try_from(...).expect(reason) documents the invariant instead of hiding it behind 'as'. The u64→i64 of seconds is genuinely fallible (year ~2.9e11 wraps to negative); try_from with a fallback to a sentinel string is the idiomatic shape.
title: now_utc_string and civil_from_days use lossy 'as' casts instead of try_from
